title: Combining Textual Features for the Identification of Duplicate Entities in Databases
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
abstract: Entity Matching (EM) is the task of identifying which records in one or more databases refer to the same real-world entity. In this paper, we propose a deep learning approach that combines multiple textual features using pre-trained language models (BERT) to improve the accuracy of entity matching across heterogeneous data sources.

title: time2feat: Extracting Interpretable Features from Multivariate Time Series
abstract: We present time2feat, a novel framework for extracting interpretable features from multivariate time series data to support clustering and classification tasks. The system automatically selects the most discriminative features while maintaining human interpretability, enabling domain experts to understand the basis of model decisions.

title: MASQ: Multi-Attribute Selectivity Estimation Using Deep Learning
venue: ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
abstract: We introduce MASQ, a system for performing ML model inference directly within database query engines. MASQ enables efficient execution of machine learning models over large datasets without data movement, leveraging query optimization techniques to minimize computational overhead.

title: AE4ND: Autoencoder-based Novelty Detection for Industrial IoT Sensor Data
venue: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
abstract: We propose AE4ND, an autoencoder-based approach for novelty detection in industrial IoT sensor streams. The system learns compact representations of normal operational patterns and identifies deviations that may signal anomalies, faults, or novel operating conditions in manufacturing environments.

title: FactFlip: Automatic Fact Verification using Contrastive Learning and Knowledge Graphs
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL)
abstract: FactFlip is a fact verification system that leverages contrastive learning and structured knowledge from knowledge graphs to assess the factual accuracy of textual claims. We demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on several benchmarks including FEVER and Climate-FEVER.

title: ClariESG: Clarifying ESG Information Extraction from Financial Documents using Large Language Models
abstract: We present ClariESG, a system for automatically extracting Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information from corporate financial documents. Our approach combines large language models with a domain-specific ontology to identify and classify ESG-related disclosures across diverse document formats.

title: UEDI: Unsupervised Evaluation Framework for Dataset Integration Methods
venue: International Conference on Database and Expert Systems Applications (DEXA)
abstract: UEDI provides a comprehensive framework for evaluating dataset integration methods in unsupervised settings where ground truth is unavailable. We propose a suite of metrics that measure integration quality from complementary perspectives: completeness, consistency, and coherence.

title: NOCTOWL: Non-parametric Online Change-point detection for Time Series with Wavelet-based Learning
venue: IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE)
abstract: NOCTOWL is a non-parametric method for detecting change points in streaming time series. The approach uses wavelet decomposition to capture multi-scale temporal patterns and employs an online learning algorithm that adapts to concept drift without requiring labeled training data.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Entity Matching over Relational Data
abstract: Entity matching — the task of identifying database records that represent the same real-world entity — is a fundamental challenge in data integration. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of entity matching techniques, covering classical blocking and matching strategies, as well as modern deep learning approaches, evaluation methodologies, and open research challenges.

title: TED4STL: Transfer and Ensemble of Deep Models for Short-Term Load Forecasting
venue: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
abstract: We present TED4STL, a framework for short-term electrical load forecasting that combines transfer learning and ensemble methods. The system adapts pre-trained temporal models to new geographic regions or building types with minimal labeled data, achieving competitive accuracy while reducing the need for extensive domain-specific training.
